sources.title: Aya Expanse 32B model card
sources.evidence: Identifies the 32-billion-parameter, open-weight multilingual text model, its CC-BY-NC-4.0 license, 23 supported languages, autoregressive Transformer architecture and 128K context. Reopened October 27, 2026: the Model Size remains 32 billion parameters. The card describes Command-family pretraining followed by supervised finetuning, preference training and model merging; it provides no separate active-parameter count.

sources.title: Aya Expanse: Connecting our world
sources.evidence: Dated October 24, 2024. The launch identifies Aya Expanse as a model family; the embedded article body explicitly links the 32B release. Page metadata gives datePublished 2024-10-24.

sources.title: Aya Expanse: Combining Research Breakthroughs for a New Multilingual Frontier
sources.evidence: The December 2024 report names the exact 32B release. Section 3 specifies 128K training context, SwiGLU, RoPE and grouped-query attention. It describes ordinary role-delimited chat training and evaluates mathematical reasoning with prompted chain of thought; it does not give a separate Aya active-parameter count. Independently rechecked the freshly fetched October 27 full report, including Section 3 and comparison tables. The only explicit active-parameter figure is 39B for Mixtral-8x22B, not Aya Expanse; the stated Command-series relationship does not identify an exact base checkpoint with a transferable active-count convention.

sources.title: Public Aya Expanse 32B repository metadata
sources.evidence: Public metadata at revision b306ea27e360683b50c005d7fcbad6a242317910 identifies CohereForCausalLM/model_type cohere. Its exact chat template supports optional system then alternating user/assistant turns, with no tools, tool_calls, tool-result or thinking serialization. The Hub reports 32,296,476,672 F16 parameters; this audit did not independently inspect their tensor headers. Fresh October 27 metadata returns the same revision and 32,296,476,672-parameter Hub total. This corroborates the nominal 32B model size without being treated as an active count.

sources.title: Cohere model implementation in Transformers 4.46.2
sources.evidence: Cohere-team implementation selected by the exact repository architecture has decoder layers with attention and a dense gated MLP (gate_proj, up_proj, down_proj), without expert routing. Read from the corresponding raw GitHub URL.

sources.title: An Overview of Cohere models
sources.evidence: Lists c4ai-aya-expanse-32b as a 32B text model with 128K context under Aya. Separately identifies Command A Reasoning as Cohere's first model with a dedicated thinking capability.

sources.title: Original Aya Expanse 32B configuration
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026: the exact original config.json still returns HTTP 401. Full configuration was not read. The published nominal 32B total does not depend on access to this file.

sources.title: Original Aya Expanse 32B checkpoint index
sources.evidence: Direct request returned HTTP 401. No shard or tensor-header count was performed.

sources.title: Aya Vision: Advancing the Frontier of Multilingual Multimodality
sources.evidence: Later May 2025 report explicitly identifies Aya-Expanse-32B as the language-model base of Aya Vision 32B. It supplies no separate active-parameter count for the original Expanse checkpoint; no vision-model properties are transferred. Independently inspected the freshly fetched October 27 full report, including Section 4.1 and comparison tables; its forward relationship to the multimodal model supplies no activated-count convention for Expanse.

sources.title: Tiny Aya: Bridging Scale and Multilingual Depth
sources.evidence: Later March 2026 report was checked for Expanse parameter disclosures. It cites Aya Expanse but supplies no separate total/active table for the exact 32B model. Independently inspected the freshly fetched October 27 full report and Table 2. Its embedding, non-embedding and total-parameter columns describe Tiny Aya, not Expanse, and do not define an Expanse active count.

sources.title: Basic usage of tool use (function calling)
sources.evidence: Describes the native tool-use interface for the Command family; it does not establish that the Aya Expanse API has that feature. The exact released template is the evidence for the checkpoint interface.

sources.title: Command A: An Enterprise-Ready Large Language Model
sources.evidence: Independently inspected the complete report from the shared October 27 primary-source fetch, searching model references and active/activated parameter terminology and checking its comparison table headings. It provides no separate Aya Expanse 32B active count or applicable dense-count convention.

sources.title: Command R7B Arabic: A Small but Mighty Arabic LLM
sources.evidence: Independently inspected the complete report from the shared October 27 primary-source fetch, including the model comparisons and parameter terminology. It gives no active-parameter disclosure for Aya Expanse 32B; its expert-model merging discussion concerns training, not an Expanse MoE active-count specification.

sources.title: Cohere Labs Model Efficiency Primer
sources.evidence: Fresh October 27 search led to this official PDF. Section 4, Trends Towards Smaller Models, explicitly calls Aya Expanse a 32bn-parameter model. It does not distinguish an Aya active-parameter count.

sources.title: Aya at a Glance
sources.evidence: Fresh October 27 search led to the official slide deck. The web reader rejected its size, so the complete 23,977,405-byte PDF was fetched directly and its text read. Slide 54 states that Aya Expanse scales to 32B parameters; the Expanse training and scaling slides provide no separate active-count definition.

sources.title: 3LM: Bridging Arabic, STEM, and Code through Benchmarking
sources.evidence: Fresh exact-model active-parameter search found this independent benchmark paper. Table 10 lists Aya Expanse size 32B and Figure 11 includes it in a plot colored by model active parameters. This is not a Cohere disclosure and provides no explicit exact-model active-count definition or parameter-count derivation. It is recorded as a search lead, not promoted to a verified developer specification.

developer.note: Developed by Cohere For AI, now Cohere Labs, the research arm of Cohere.

family.note: The launch and technical report explicitly call Aya Expanse a model family.

release_date.note: Explicit public launch date. Repository creation on October 23 is not evidence of public release that day; the December report is later.

open_weights.note: Weights are released for research under gated license acceptance.

license.note: Repository license declaration; the card additionally requires adherence to the Cohere Labs Acceptable Use Policy.

parameters_b.note: Fresh October 27 checks confirm Cohere's nominal total of 32B in the exact model card, original report, later official primer and slide deck. Public Hub metadata reports 32.296476672B; the catalog preserves the developer's published nominal precision. No tensor census is required to support this count.

active_parameters_b.note: Fresh exact-name searches and independently inspected original/later first-party reports found no separate active count or applicable developer convention. The original report's 39B active figure belongs to Mixtral; Tiny Aya's non-embedding column describes another model. The independent 3LM plot labels model size as active parameters but supplies no Cohere disclosure or exact-model derivation. Dense architecture and generic Command-family lineage alone do not establish the active field.

architecture.note: Autoregressive decoder-only Transformer with GQA, RoPE and SwiGLU. Dense classification follows the exact repository's CohereForCausalLM implementation, whose decoder MLP has no expert routing.

context_window.note: The model card, report and exact API model row advertise 128K context; preserved as nominal 128,000 tokens. The gated configuration was not available to check its internal position limit.

modalities.note: The exact card explicitly specifies text-only input and output.

reasoning.note: No dedicated thinking mode in this released checkpoint's chat format. Reported chain-of-thought benchmark performance describes ordinary prompted text reasoning; Cohere distinguishes dedicated thinking models in its model documentation.

tool_call.note: No native tool-call interface in the released checkpoint: its template serializes only system/user/assistant text and has no tool definitions, tool-call fields or tool-result handling. This does not claim an inability to emit tool-like text when prompted.

description.value: Open-weight multilingual text model supporting 23 languages.
description.note: Plain summary of documented modality, access and language coverage.

patch.description: Open-weight multilingual text model supporting 23 languages.

sources.label: Aya Expanse: Combining Research Breakthroughs for a New Multilingual Frontier

patch.notes: 32B is Cohere's nominal total; active parameters are not separately disclosed. Context is advertised as 128K. The released template provides ordinary text chat without dedicated thinking or native tool-call formatting. The CC-BY-NC-4.0 release includes Cohere Labs' Acceptable Use Addendum.

summary: October 27 parameter re-audit confirms the published nominal 32B total. Fresh exact-model searches, the model card and metadata, original and later Cohere reports, official primer and slide deck yielded no separate developer active-count disclosure. The independent 3LM active-parameter chart was checked as a lead but does not establish Cohere's counting convention. Retained active_parameters_b as undisclosed, added explicit parameter patches, and preserved all unrelated assessments.
